description: Justified assumptions allowed in the transitive closure of the accepted bridge theorems (verification/lean/ClosureAudit.lean). Each entry is a full-match regular expression over declaration names with its justification. Anything in the closure that no entry matches rejects acceptance.

axioms.justification: Lean foundational axiom: global choice (classical logic, used by Mathlib analysis for fderiv).
Lean foundational axiom: quotient soundness (implies function extensionality).

opaque.justification: `irreducible_def` wrapper (Mathlib.Tactic.IrreducibleDef): an opaque value of the subtype {x // x = definition}; the property fixes the value, so the constant hides no freedom. Used by Mathlib (Real arithmetic, Asymptotics, FDeriv, TangentCone, Filter) and by Aeneas scalar bounds.

Lean core platform word size, only known to be 32 or 64. Aeneas usize bounds depend on it, so every theorem holds for both widths (more general than the arm64/x86_64 native targets, which are 64-bit).

Rust build configuration `cfg!(ub_checks)` (the `ub_checks` intrinsic that guards core's `assert_unsafe_precondition!` checks). It follows `debug_assertions`: native tests and debug builds run the checks, release builds do not. Aeneas translates MIR `NullaryOp(UbChecks)` to this opaque Bool, so every theorem holds for both configurations. Compiled evaluation (#eval/#guard) uses the default `false`, which is never counted as proof.

Lean core identity kept opaque for compilation. Witness path: proof terms of Lean core `grind` commutative-ring normalization (Lean.Grind.CommRing.Mon.revlexWF, well-founded recursion) used inside Mathlib lemma proofs; it occurs in proofs, not in any stated model definition.

Lean core String primitives opaque in Lean v4.29. Witness path: mkPanicMessageWithDecl <- panicWithPosWithDecl <- List.get!Internal (panic-message construction; kernel semantics of a panic return the default value, so the message string never affects a theorem).

Platform libm: values unconstrained; no accepted theorem may depend on them. `f32`/`f64` `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `atan`, `exp` and `ln` call the platform libm, whose results are not correctly rounded and differ between platforms and libm versions, so each is an opaque function with no axiom about its values (Aeneas.Std.Float); their compiled stand-in returns a NaN, so no evaluation through them is evidence. Reached by chelis-types dtype_semantics.rs:1011 apply_float_unop_f32 and :1036 apply_float_unop_f64 (FloatUnOp Exp/Log/Sin/Cos/Tan/Atan), the ActivationElement exp impls (:2112, and :2145 through f32 for f16/bf16) used by activation_sigmoid (:2167), and chelis-ir optimize.rs:117-123 (constant folding of RiscOp Exp/Log/Sin/Cos/Tan/Atan).

extern.justification: Lean core compiled implementations (@[extern]/@[implemented_by]). The kernel checks proofs against the Lean definitions; the compiled code matters only for evaluation-based evidence (#guard/#eval), which is never counted as proof.
Lean core panic reporting for compiled code; kernel semantics return the default value.

platform_assumptions.assumption: Native code runs on aarch64, where rustc lowers f32/f64 max/min to LLVM maxnum/minnum and the backend selects FMAXNM/FMINNM with FPCR.DN = 0.
platform_assumptions.justification: Rust leaves the sign of a zero result (max(-0.0, +0.0)) and NaN payloads unspecified, so no target-independent model is exact. The model is the Arm ARM FPMaxNum/FPMinNum bit for bit (-0 < +0; a quiet NaN yields the other operand; a signaling NaN yields itself quieted) and verification/float_std_models.rs and float_model_oracle.rs check it bit for bit against native code on the build host, including every signed-zero and NaN case. x86-64 lowers maxnum differently; the correspondence is claimed for aarch64 only. Reached by chelis-ir eval.rs:376 (dropout scale `1.0 / (1.0 - rate.max(0.0))`) and chelis-types fitness.rs:111 (`(unresolved_count as f64 / total as f64).min(1.0)`).

platform_assumptions.assumption: Native code runs on aarch64 with the fp16 feature (every Apple silicon host), where half 2.7.1 dispatches f16::from_f64 to FCVT Hd, Dd.
platform_assumptions.justification: FCVT is the correctly rounded IEEE conversion (round to nearest, ties to even), which the model defines as BinaryFloat.cast, with Arm FPConvertNaN payloads. The crate's software fallback (hosts without fp16/f16c) truncates the low 32 bits of the f64 first and x86 f16c converts through f32; both round twice and differ from the model on some inputs. verification/crate_model_oracle (half_model_oracle) checks the model against the crate on edge cases and dense per-exponent samples. Reached by chelis-types dtype_semantics.rs:2138 (`<half::f16 as ActivationElement>::constant`, from impl_reduced_activation_element!(half::f16) at :2164), which float_vec_activation (:2176) calls for the Sigmoid/Tanh/GELU constants on F16 buffers (:2248), among them 0.044715 and 0.7978845608028654, which are not exactly representable in f16.

admission_assumptions.assumption: An Ord impl that carries #[automatically_derived] is rustc's #[derive(Ord)] expansion.
admission_assumptions.justification: The sort_unstable/sort_unstable_by models are exact only where Equal holds exactly for indistinguishable values. SortContracts admits a crate element type only if its Ord impl carries #[automatically_derived], which rustc puts on derive expansions and Charon (since 5fd1554) keeps as an unknown attribute, and every field type is admitted: the derived cmp compares the variants, then the fields in order. Rust also accepts the attribute on a hand-written impl, which is where this assumption lies; no retained production crate writes it (`automatically_derived` does not occur in crates/). Reached by chelis-types linearity.rs:311 (`ids.sort_unstable()` on Vec<BindingId>; BindingId derives Ord over u32 at linearity.rs:161).
